subject: Post-demo: BloomCare model fit & function call qualification
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@bloomcare.ai>, Tom Li <tom.li@bloomcare.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo recap + proposed next steps

Hi Samira and Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time to go through the demo this morning — appreciated the candid feedback on the structured discharge summaries use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Highlights from the call:
- Goal: high-precision structured summaries for discharge notes with strict JSON schema enforcement and low false-positive field population.
- Volume estimate: ~30k clinical events / month across pilot clinics.
- Quality bar: >95% schema compliance for required fields; human-in-the-loop fallback for ambiguous cases.

Proposed next steps (action items):
1) Redwood: run a model-fit eval using the prompt-set we captured in the call + sample data you shared. Deliverables: benchmark report, hit/miss examples, and suggested schema for retries.
2) BloomCare: confirm procurement contact and timing for pilot PO; share any data residency constraints.
3) Tech sync: schedule a 30-min session next week with your engineering lead to validate function-call shapes and webhook behavior.

Attachments: demo recording (bloomcare-demo-recording.mp4), prompt set (prompt-set-v1.csv).

I'll kick off the model-fit eval today and tag Dylan to lead the technical evaluation.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com

From: Samira Khan <samira@bloomcare.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Li <tom.li@bloomcare.ai>, procurement@bloomcare.ai
Date: 2027-06-21T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + proposed next steps

Thanks Naomi — great summary.

We can confirm procurement contact is procurement@bloomcare.ai (Amy Rogers will own the PO). Expected timeline: internal approval by 7/8, PO by ~7/15 if no surprises. Data residency: US only for pilot.

For the tech sync, please include details on function calls (we need explicit examples of the webhook payload and retry semantics). Tom suggested an internal 30-min sync on 6/23 at 10am PT. Does that work?

Also looping in: one quick ask from product — can you include a short baseline that compares two model families you expect to recommend (one smaller quantized model and one high-capacity model) so we can evaluate cost vs. precision trade-offs?

Thanks,
Samira
VP Product, BloomCare

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-22T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Post-demo recap + proposed next steps

Hi team — I started the fit eval against the sample set Samira uploaded. Quick notes and what I'll deliver by EOD 6/24: 

1) Models to include in the benchmark (recommended):
   - Redwood-Standard-7B-8bit (quantized, cost-efficient) — expect faster turnaround and good structural compliance on required fields.
   - LlamaX-13B-finetuned (high-capacity) — higher precision on ambiguous text spans; larger latency.

2) Eval plan and metrics:
   - Schema compliance (primary): percent of outputs that match required JSON types & required keys.
   - Field-level F1 for named entities (diagnosis, medication, discharge_instructions).
   - Latency P50/P95 for 512-token context, and cost per 1k tokens.

3) Function-calling / JSON schema approach:
   - We'll validate outputs against the attached schema-example.json and add an explicit wrapper that returns either {"result": <object>} or {"error": "validation_failed", "errors": [..]} when the model produces invalid JSON.
   - Retry policy: up to 2 automated retries with temperature 0.0 and incremental system prompt guidance to prefer strict schema filling. On repeated failures, route to human review queue.

4) Sample benchmarks (preliminary, small sample):
   - Redwood-Standard-7B-8bit: schema compliance 88% (small fixes often needed for nested arrays)
   - LlamaX-13B: schema compliance 96% but median latency ~180ms higher per request in our private tests

Deliverables on 6/24: full benchmark CSV, example prompts used (prompt-set-v1.csv attached), failure examples, and suggested minimal schema tweaks to reduce false positives.

I'll join the 6/23 tech sync; Naomi — can you confirm invite?

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: schema-example.json (validation schema), prompt-set-v1.csv
From: Tom Li <tom.li@bloomcare.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira@bloomcare.ai>, procurement@bloomcare.ai
Date: 2027-06-24T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + proposed next steps

Appreciate the quick turnaround. The preliminary numbers look promising — the tradeoffs you called out align with what we expected. A few asks before procurement moves forward: 

- Can you include a short section in the benchmark that quantifies the cost delta at expected throughput (30k events/month) for each model? That will help our finance team.
- Please confirm expected SLA for P95 latency if we run on Dedicated vs Hosted. We may aim for Dedicated for pilot if SLA is within 300ms P95.
- Security: Amy (procurement) will request SOC 2 Type II evidence and an export-control table for where data may be cached.

If those items are packaged with the final eval on 6/24 we can proceed to procurement review on 7/6.

Thanks — Tom
Head of Engineering, BloomCare
